critic_notes: All 12 cards re-verified on the current tree (every cited path:line read; all 54 receiving-file LOC counts match the cards' loc_check). No card re-proposes a 2026-10-05 card, a BACKLOG.md row, a run-1/run-2 (landed) or a run-3 (building) card. Cross-run write-set overlap with run-3 is flagged per card and in `overlaps`.

rulings.developer_A_policy_loosen: NOT policy-loosen; in-scope `contract`. Reasons: (1) no existing row changes exposure — the column defaults false and a share without a consent section saves false, so every stored share stays out; (2) what crosses upward is a contribution to a floor-cleared aggregate and only that (aggregate-vs-individual-split: 'Individual values may not cross upward ... What crosses upward is a contribution to an aggregate, and only that'); private-view-separation's 'may not become one by being harvested' is answered by explicit per-share consent as data the producer filters on, not by convention; (3) suppression is producer-enforced (CHAMPION_MIN_POP, CARE_BAND_MIN_SHARERS, k-floor on free-text kept-move titles) and the cohort read returns no login; (4) the product's own contract already names this path as opt-in ('Opt-in — and off is a decision, not a gap', CareWhyStrip.tsx:103) and records C4 as a Known gap (developer.md:281-283). It stores one boolean more per share (the consent itself) and sends nothing person-shaped. Condition that must hold at build: the consent flag is writable only through the owner-self POST (it is), the cohort reader is the only non-self reader of MentorShare and it selects payloadJson only where orgAggregate=true, and the revoke path (re-POST without consent, or DELETE) takes effect on the next aggregate read.
rulings.retention: Neither retention card deletes more, shortens a horizon or rewrites history. A is a pure relocation behind an unchanged PurgeSummary contract with preview==delete pinned; B is read-only plus an additive response field. A is revised (not voided) to pin the relocated predicates against today's inline ones so 'deletes no more' is a test, not an intent.
rulings.mcp_github_app_external_contracts: mcp A: MCP wire unchanged (runTool gains an optional trailing arg; tools/list bytes untouched); the holder-required set must stay a superset of today's three. mcp B: result shapes and keys unchanged, `_meta` keys namespaced and additive, redaction only narrows what leaves; the catalog's org-authored set is pinned to ATHENA_UNTRUSTED_TOOLS. github-app A: HMAC verification, bounded read, dedup claim and the 24h horizon untouched; the App manifest and subscription table are not edited; the two closed arms bind on the STORED mapping only and mint no token. github-app B: the repo secret NAMES (ASCENT_CONFORMANCE_URL / ASCENT_CONFORMANCE_TOKEN) and the token scope (telemetry:write) are unchanged; only the org-token name becomes per-repo, so a credential's reach narrows.

verdicts.title: C4: one consent-keyed producer feeds the org care aggregate and your bands
verdicts.ambition_why: Lands the designed-but-starved half of the care loop with consent as data and suppression in the producer — the move the standard prescribes, not a tidy-up.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor holds: getCareOrgAggregate returns emptyOrgView (load.ts:133-136), careBandFromSharers has no production caller, orgBands is written by no loader, TOP has no consent key, MentorShare is keyed by login only, the doc records C4 as a Known gap.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: 8 cases, 7 red before; the Prisma-where assertion (orgAggregate:true AND member logins) and the no-login JSON assertion are the two that would catch a wrong build; case 7 is green-before by design and honestly labelled.
verdicts.notes: Ruling: in-scope contract, not policy-loosen (see rulings.developer_A_policy_loosen). Overlap with run-3: prisma/schema.prisma is also edited by oauth B and providers A (all additive models), and the migration dir 20261023120000_mentor_share_org_aggregate shares its timestamp with both run-3 migrations — distinct names so Prisma accepts it, but pick a later timestamp when building to keep ordering unambiguous. developer-view.ts is already 373 lines (.ts, spirit-only); the card correctly keeps new derivations out of it.

verdicts.grounding_why: Every button is console.info (CareBits.tsx:47/60), both Share actions are unwired, DELETE exists with no caller, validateCareShare is pure (no db import), BACKLOG #22 is concept-doc first. One immaterial misline: careShareLedger is at care-share-view.ts:25, not :161 (the file is 53 lines).
verdicts.falsifiability_why: 8 cases all red before; the 'same validator as the route' case and the demo-view-disables-commit case are the ones that bite; the fetch-count assertions pin single POST/DELETE.
verdicts.notes: All new files under src/features/developer stay under 200. No overlap with run-3. Pairs naturally with card A (consent toggling needs a re-POST, which this card makes possible) but shares no file with it.

verdicts.revise: Scope the doc-table guard (acceptance case 6) to backtick tokens in the FIRST column of the event table in docs/features/github/github-app.md:94-104 — the action cells also backtick function names (`upsertInstallation`, `reconcileInstallationRepos`, `runPushRescan`, `onRegistryPush`, `isRepoAutoscanned` ...), so 'every backtick in the table' can never equal the arm set and the guard would be loosened at build time.

verdicts.grounding_why: route.ts:796-809 runs attribution after a void-returning enqueueControlProbe that abandons on mismatch (:323-326); reduceAiChangeEvent (:438-492) and recordControlAttribution (:385-422) never call installationMatchesOwner (grep: 143 def, 233, 323, 497, 525, 781); pr-gate.ts:48 confirmOwner optional; route.test.ts has zero recordObservations/upsertLiveAiChange pins.

verdicts.notes: External contract: HMAC verification, bounded read, dedup claim, 24h horizon and the subscription table untouched; the two closed arms bind on the stored mapping only (no token minted, no GitHub call) so nothing a token reads widens. Write set is 2 edited + 8 new files, all .ts outside src/features; route.test.ts at 1469 lines is unchanged except imports (its module mocks still intercept relocated code). No run-3 overlap.

verdicts.title: Report-back you can trust: one credential per repo, broken rows named + fixable
verdicts.ambition_why: Finds a real silent fleet failure (N provisioned repos, 1 working credential) and fixes it at the credential model plus the row state — the fix is on the row, not a banner.
verdicts.grounding_why: TOKEN_NAME is one name (route.ts:42); rotate:true before any secret write (:151-156); org-api-tokens.ts:163-167 retires every live token of the name; audit row written with ok:false (:180-191); getFoundationRollout never reads meta.ok (org-foundation.ts:88-108); DELETE revokes the shared name (:227); marks are Provisioned/Not provisioned only; route.test.ts:209/:257 pin today's behaviour.

verdicts.notes: policy-tighten verified: secret names and token scope unchanged, so external CI needs no change; a leaked repo secret now exposes one repo's credential. No name-length constraint exists in org-api-tokens.ts, so the 80-char bound is a self-imposed sanity cap, fine. 12 edited + 2 new = 14 files, at the ceiling but every features file stays under 200. No run-3 overlap. Doc sync: github-app.md:314 must stop saying 'named conformance report-back'.

verdicts.title: Purge ledgers as one declared table: preview becomes a mode of the deleter
verdicts.revise: Add one pin to retention-ledgers.test.ts: a snapshot test that each PURGE_LEDGERS descriptor's where(orgId, cutoff) deep-equals the predicate purgeExpiredData uses today for that ledger — usageEvent {orgId, createdAt:{lt}}, conformanceReport {orgId, reportedAt:{lt}} with findings via report, orgMemoryCitation {orgId, createdAt:{lt}}, and the controlObservation keep-newest-per-(repoFullName, controlId) rule with `lt` (never `lte`) at the cutoff — so 'deletes no more than today' is asserted against the old predicates, not only preview==delete (which both could drift together).
verdicts.ambition_why: Declares each purged ledger once and derives preview, delete, result row, audit meta and rollup from it, closing a recorded registry deviation — the right move on a 2808-line module.
verdicts.grounding_why: Dry-run counts at :914-926 and findMany predicates at :1044/:1071/:1107 are hand-copied twins; erase-side drain closure at :1800-1811; usageEventsDeleted named 13 times inside purgeExpiredData (17 in the file); :1005 adds counts only after pruneRepoScans returns; registry-map carries the :1005 deviation; dry-run-preview.md:22 states 'a mode of the deleter'.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 2-3 (committed counts survive a throw) and 5 (an appended descriptor is counted and deleted with no edit to purgeExpiredData) are red before and specific; the two guards are green before and honestly labelled; the missing pin is the revise.
verdicts.notes: Ruling: deletes no more data, shortens no horizon, rewrites no history — pure relocation behind an unchanged purgeExpiredData/PurgeSummary contract; budget checks, floor refusal, rotation and orphan/queue/quota sweeps untouched. Overlap: retention.ts was edited by run-2 security A (landed, audit-append door) — rebase on master, not on an older read. No run-3 overlap.

All features files stay under 200 (RetentionCard.test.tsx 109 -> ~170). No overlap with retention A (A edits retention.ts/retention-policy.ts; B reads OrgPurgeResult's type only). No run-3 overlap.

verdicts.grounding_why: registry-map pair is state deviation, stale:true, revisionsBehind 3; handlers.ts:432-467 is the 16-arm switch with per-arm principal ternaries; grounding.ts:4-6/163-165 keep the stale 'until the handler uses the same packer' premise while handlers.ts:334 uses recallMemories and :311 filters terms before the cap (47d10a70, 95105469 both in log); PRINCIPAL_SCOPE heuristic at :139; McpPlanGate declared in both tools.ts:44 and gates.ts:23.

verdicts.notes: External contract: tools/list bytes and tool result shapes unchanged; runTool gains only an optional trailing options arg; no token reads more. Write-set overlap with run-3 followups A on src/lib/mcp/handlers.ts (and its premise rests on the switch that card edits) — hence the revise. No overlap with mcp B's edited files (B edits tools.ts and route.ts; A edits handlers.ts, gates.ts, write-gate.ts, grounding.ts).

verdicts.title: Org-authored tool results leave the agent door redacted, with provenance _meta
verdicts.ambition_why: Applies the house egress rule at the one door that skipped it and makes result trust a declared catalog fact — the two doors can no longer disagree on the same rule.
verdicts.grounding_why: untrusted.ts:44-48 states the rule; grounding.ts:300 fences ATHENA_UNTRUSTED_TOOLS; route.ts:305-313 returns text and structuredContent verbatim; grep for redact/sanitize/wrapUntrusted in src/lib/mcp and src/app/api/mcp is empty; registry-reads.ts:154/:197 and handlers.ts:362 forward foreign-authored fields; redactSecrets at redact.ts:74.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: 6 red-before cases on concrete credential shapes plus the byte-identical get_repo_standing guard; the shape-preservation case (numbers/booleans/nulls untouched) and the contentHash-vs-redactions case catch the two ways this is built wrong.
verdicts.notes: External contract: result keys and shapes unchanged, `_meta` keys namespaced and additive, redaction only narrows egress — policy-tighten holds. Quality risk to carry into the build: redactSecrets' assignment-shape patterns can mask legitimate example code in skill bodies (e.g. `API_KEY=...` in a how-to); Athena already applies the same masker to the same five tools, so this is parity, not new mangling, and the redactions count makes it visible. Write-set overlap with run-3 followups A on src/lib/mcp/tools.ts (schema edits for report_attempt) and src/app/api/mcp/route.ts (McpPrincipal) — land after it; no premise of this card rests on the lines that card changes.
